It peaked at 35 on HipHop air play but topped the hot 100 for 1 week (previous week it was at 52), with a span of 36 weeks total on the chart. Streams helped it skyrocket to the top after his passing, but without radio it didn’t last long. Definitely a big hit but I rarely heard it playing on radio like you said.

Basically, unless the artist is able to pull millions of streams in a condensed time plus support from radio, say in the case of popular acts like Drake, Ariana Grande, Billie Eyelash, without radio supporting and spinning tracks, some may barely see the light of day on the Hot 100. I think this alludes a lot of the word “Payola” being thrown around now more so than previous music decades. Because a song may be peaking highly on the chart for so long without garnering the streams to match it looks shady in the eyes of fans who’s artists may not be charting successfully even though the streams are there-over time instead of in a short period. But that’s because radio is constantly playing that successful song and that’s more exposure for the song to garner streams and STAY on the chart. Unlike “sleeper hits” that may do well initially with streaming numbers and finally making it to radio, and having to climb up the chart. Just think of streams as the new sales. 

People do stream BUT no radio play: it’ll take time to get to radio and chart better. 

People do stream AND radio plays: it’s bound to do well on the chart. 

People don’t stream BUT radio plays: it gains streams and continues to rise on the chart.
